summary: List, get, summarize, and stop time entries

get.summary: Show a single time entry by ID (full field set).

list.summary: List time entries of a time range (default: today), or show the running clock entry.
list.usage: clockodo entries list [--me|--user <id>] [--since <date>] [--until <date>] | clockodo entries list --running

options.name: --me
options.description: Only entries of the authenticated user. Exclusive with --user.

options.name: --user
options.description: Only entries of this user. Exclusive with --me.

options.name: --since
options.description: Start of the range, inclusive (local day or UTC timestamp).

options.name: --until
options.description: End of the range; a local day includes the whole day.

options.name: --running
options.description: Show the running clock entry of the authenticated user. Not combinable with the other options.

list.requests: GET /v2/entries (enhanced list, paginated, not cached, rate limit 300 requests / 15 min); --me adds GET /v4/users/me; --running uses GET /v2/clock
list.data: Array of time entry objects (unwrapped from .entries); with --running the /v2/clock response.

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: Clock entry ID. Without it the running entry of the authenticated user is looked up.

stop.requests: DELETE /v2/clock/{id}; without an ID GET /v2/clock first
notes: --dry-run runs the lookup and reports the DELETE without sending it.
stop.data: API response without data wrapper; the stopped entry is in .stopped.

summary.summary: Day summary of one user: total time incl. the running entry, start of day, target hours, delta, percent.

options.name: --me
options.description: Summary of the authenticated user. Exclusive with --user.

options.name: --user
options.description: Summary of this user. Exclusive with --me.

summary.requests: GET /v2/entries for the day; GET /targethours and (with --me) GET /v4/users/me, both cached with CACHE=1
summary.data: {date, users_id, current_time, count_entries, total_seconds, start_of_day, running, target_seconds, delta_seconds, percent}; all durations in seconds, target fields null without a weekly rule.
